### Outputs

The following code reads the two previously downloaded data files from the working directory, recalculates the estimates, and produces the revised figures and OLS growth-rate estimates. It does not require objects created by earlier code chunks.

#### Data location

The data files are expected to be in the folder from which Quarto renders this document. The code checks for existing files before downloading them.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# #### 1. Check packages and locate the data

pkgs <- c("data.table", "ggplot2", "viridis")

have <- rownames(installed.packages())
miss <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% have]

if (length(miss) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install these packages in the R console first: ",
    "install.packages(c(",
    paste(shQuote(miss), collapse = ", "),
    "))"
  )
}

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

cat("Working directory:", normalizePath(getwd()), "\n")

bl_file <- "BL_v3_MF.csv"
un_file <- "HDR23-24_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv"

cat("Barro-Lee file exists:", file.exists(bl_file), "\n")
cat("UNDP file exists:", file.exists(un_file), "\n")

# #### 2. Download only files that are missing

if (!file.exists(bl_file)) {
  download.file(
    paste0(
      "https://barrolee.github.io/",
      "BarroLeeDataSet/BLData/",
      bl_file
    ),
    bl_file,
    mode = "wb"
  )
}

if (!file.exists(un_file)) {
  download.file(
    paste0(
      "https://hdr.undp.org/sites/default/",
      "files/2023-24_HDR/",
      un_file
    ),
    un_file,
    mode = "wb"
  )
}

# Confirm that both files are now available.
stopifnot(file.exists(bl_file), file.exists(un_file))

cat("Barro-Lee:", normalizePath(bl_file), "\n")
cat("UNDP:", normalizePath(un_file), "\n")

# #### 3. Read and prepare the data

bl <- fread(bl_file)
un <- fread(un_file)

# Barro-Lee: population-weighted mean for ages 25-64.
bla <- bl[agefrom >= 25]

blc <- bla[, .(
  mys = sum(yr_sch * pop, na.rm = TRUE) /
    sum(pop[!is.na(yr_sch)], na.rm = TRUE),
  pop = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(country, year, region = region_code)]

# Remove rows that cannot contribute to the estimates.
blc <- blc[is.finite(mys) & is.finite(pop) & pop > 0]

# UNDP: retain country records, not aggregate records.
unc <- un[!grepl("^ZZ", iso3)]

mys_cols <- grep("^mys_[0-9]{4}$", names(unc), value = TRUE)
pop_cols <- grep("^pop_total_[0-9]{4}$", names(unc), value = TRUE)

m1 <- melt(
  unc,
  id.vars = c("country", "region"),
  measure.vars = mys_cols,
  variable.name = "year",
  value.name = "mys"
)
m1[, year := as.integer(sub("mys_", "", year))]

p1 <- melt(
  unc,
  id.vars = "country",
  measure.vars = pop_cols,
  variable.name = "year",
  value.name = "pop"
)
p1[, year := as.integer(sub("pop_total_", "", year))]

unl <- merge(m1, p1, by = c("country", "year"))

reg_names <- c(
  AS = "Arab States",
  EAP = "East Asia and the Pacific",
  ECA = "Europe and Central Asia",
  LAC = "Latin America and the Caribbean",
  SA = "South Asia",
  SSA = "Sub-Saharan Africa"
)

unl[, region := reg_names[region]]
unl[is.na(region), region := "No UNDP region"]
unl <- unl[is.finite(mys) & is.finite(pop) & pop > 0]

# #### 4. Calculate weighted means and bootstrap intervals

boot_mean <- function(d, B = 1000) {
  m <- dcast(d, country ~ year, value.var = "mys")
  w <- dcast(d, country ~ year, value.var = "pop")

  yrs <- as.integer(names(m)[-1])
  m <- as.matrix(m[, -1])
  w <- as.matrix(w[, -1])

  w[is.na(m) | is.na(w)] <- 0
  m[is.na(m)] <- 0

  est <- colSums(m * w) / colSums(w)

  draws <- matrix(NA_real_, B, ncol(m))
  set.seed(20261008)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    i <- sample(seq_len(nrow(m)), nrow(m), replace = TRUE)
    draws[b, ] <- colSums(m[i, , drop = FALSE] *
      w[i, , drop = FALSE]) /
      colSums(w[i, , drop = FALSE])
  }

  data.table(
    year = yrs,
    mys = est,
    lo = apply(draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi = apply(draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

bl_wld <- boot_mean(blc)
un_wld <- boot_mean(unl)

# Regional estimates are population-weighted means.
weighted_mean <- function(d) {
  d[, .(
    mys = sum(mys * pop) / sum(pop)
  ), by = .(year, region)]
}

bl_reg <- weighted_mean(blc)
un_reg <- weighted_mean(unl)

# #### 5. Prepare the world series

bl_wld[, source := "Barro-Lee (25-64)"]
un_wld[, source := "UNDP HDR (25+)"]

wld <- rbindlist(list(bl_wld, un_wld), use.names = TRUE)

# #### 6. Figure 1: world estimates with 95% intervals

p_world <- ggplot(
  wld,
  aes(x = year, y = mys, colour = source, fill = source)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    alpha = 0.20,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1. Mean years of schooling worldwide",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean years of schooling",
    colour = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_world)

# #### 7. Figures 2 and 3: regional estimates without intervals

p_bl <- ggplot(
  bl_reg,
  aes(x = year, y = mys, colour = region, shape = region)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  scale_shape_discrete() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2. Barro-Lee regional estimates",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean years of schooling, ages 25-64",
    colour = "Region",
    shape = "Region",
    caption = "Source: Barro-Lee v3"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2),
         shape = guide_legend(ncol = 2))

print(p_bl)

p_un <- ggplot(
  un_reg,
  aes(x = year, y = mys, colour = region, shape = region)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  scale_shape_discrete() +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 3. UNDP regional estimates",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean years of schooling, ages 25+",
    colour = "Region",
    shape = "Region",
    caption = "Source: UNDP HDR 2023/24"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2),
         shape = guide_legend(ncol = 2))

print(p_un)

# #### 8. Estimate annual growth rates by OLS

# The dependent variable is log(mean years of schooling).
# The slope therefore estimates a compound annual growth rate.
# The confidence interval is based on the OLS standard error.

growth_data <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(
    year = bl_wld$year,
    mys = bl_wld$mys,
    source = "Barro-Lee",
    series = "World"
  ),
  data.table(
    year = un_wld$year,
    mys = un_wld$mys,
    source = "UNDP",
    series = "World"
  ),
  data.table(
    year = bl_reg$year,
    mys = bl_reg$mys,
    source = "Barro-Lee",
    series = bl_reg$region
  ),
  data.table(
    year = un_reg$year,
    mys = un_reg$mys,
    source = "UNDP",
    series = un_reg$region
  )
))

growth_data <- growth_data[
  is.finite(mys) & mys > 0 & is.finite(year)
]

keys <- unique(growth_data[, .(source, series)])
growth_results <- vector("list", nrow(keys))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(keys))) {
  d <- growth_data[
    source == keys$source[i] &
      series == keys$series[i]
  ]

  fit <- lm(log(mys) ~ year, data = d)
  b <- coef(fit)["year"]
  ci <- confint(fit, "year", level = 0.95)

  growth_results[[i]] <- data.table(
    source = keys$source[i],
    series = keys$series[i],
    first_year = min(d$year),
    last_year = max(d$year),
    annual_growth_percent = 100 * (exp(b) - 1),
    ci_lower = 100 * (exp(ci[1]) - 1),
    ci_upper = 100 * (exp(ci[2]) - 1),
    observations = nrow(d)
  )
}

growth_table <- rbindlist(growth_results)

growth_table[, `:=`(
  estimate_and_95CI = sprintf(
    "%.3f%% [%.3f%%, %.3f%%]",
    annual_growth_percent, ci_lower, ci_upper
  )
)]

# #### 9. Output the growth-rate estimates

growth_output <- growth_table[, .(
  Source = source,
  Region = series,
  Period = paste(first_year, last_year, sep = "-"),
  `Annual growth rate [95% CI]` = estimate_and_95CI,
  Years = observations
)]

growth_output <- growth_output[
  order(Source, Region)
]

print(growth_output)

# #### 10. Data coverage and regional counts

coverage <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(
    Source = "Barro-Lee",
    Countries = uniqueN(blc$country),
    First_year = min(blc$year),
    Last_year = max(blc$year),
    Regions = uniqueN(blc$region)
  ),
  data.table(
    Source = "UNDP HDR",
    Countries = uniqueN(unl$country),
    First_year = min(unl$year),
    Last_year = max(unl$year),
    Regions = uniqueN(unl$region)
  )
))

print(coverage)
```

**Interpretation of the OLS output:** each estimate is the fitted annual percentage growth rate in mean years of schooling, with its 95% confidence interval in brackets. This is a log-linear trend over the available years, not a year-by-year growth rate. The intervals reflect OLS uncertainty under the regression assumptions.
